title: How Many Days Do You Need in Türkiye for Veneers, Crowns or Implants?

metaDescription: How many days you need in Türkiye for veneers, crowns, implants, or sinus lifts—including lab try-ins and safe post-surgery flight buffers.
quickAnswer: Plan 6–8 working days in Türkiye for 16–20 crowns or veneers, 5–7 days for Visit 1 of dental implants, and 7–10 days for Visit 2 permanent bridges. Sinus lifts or major bone grafts require longer recovery buffers before flying—at least 10–14 days—based on your surgeon's clearance.

How many working days do 16–20 crowns or veneers require?

A full smile restoration of 16 to 20 crowns or veneers typically requires six to eight working days—roughly eight to ten calendar days once arrival, Sunday lab closures, and a post-bonding bite check are included. That timeframe allows proper tooth preparation, digital scanning, ceramic layering, shade try-ins, and occlusion refinement.

Remember that Turkish dental laboratories normally pause or operate reduced shifts on Sundays and public holidays. Booking a Monday-morning first consultation with a Tuesday or Wednesday departure the following week gives technicians uninterrupted production days and leaves 24 hours after final cementation to test your bite on real food. For material trade-offs that affect laboratory steps, see our [zirconia vs E-max guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/zirconia-vs-emax-turkey).

body.text: Why should you never rush lab trials and bite adjustments into 3 days?

Compressing 16–20 crowns or veneers into three days eliminates essential try-in stages, forcing technicians to mill monolithic blocks quickly without verifying gum margins, phonetics, or jaw alignment. Even a fraction-of-a-millimetre high spot on a crown can trigger jaw pain, chipped porcelain, or nerve irritation once you return home.

A [British Dental Association (BDA) survey](https://www.bda.org/representation/priorities/improving-oral-health/dental-tourism/) found that 86% of UK dentists who examined dental tourists had treated post-trip complications, with poorly fitted crowns ranking as the single most common problem. A safe schedule includes:

items: Day 1: Clinical exam, X-rays/CBCT, mock-up, and tooth preparation
Days 2–4: Laboratory milling, hand-layering, and temporary wear
Day 5: Biscuit try-in (checking shape, shade in natural daylight, speech, and bite)
Day 6–7: Final glazing, permanent cementation, and nightguard impression
Day 8: Follow-up occlusion check before heading to the airport

body.text: How long do you stay for sinus lift or bone grafting?

Simple minor bone grafting placed alongside an implant usually fits inside a five-to-seven-day surgical stay, whereas an open lateral sinus lift requires a significantly longer stay—commonly ten to fourteen days before boarding a commercial flight—plus a four-to-six-month healing wait before final implants or bridges are loaded.

Because a sinus lift raises the delicate Schneiderian membrane, sneezing, nose-blowing, or cabin pressure drops can disturb the graft. Two-stage grafting may extend our [All-on-4 and All-on-6 two-visit timeline](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/dental-implants-turkey-timeline); confirm an oral surgeon via our [dentist verification checklist](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/verify-dentist-turkey).
When is it safe to fly after oral surgery?

Published clinical guidance recommends waiting at least 24 hours after crowns or veneers, 24 to 48 hours after simple extractions, at least 72 hours (with one week preferred) after surgical extractions or dental implant placement, and at least two weeks after a sinus lift before flying—always subject to your surgeon's sign-off.

A [2023 clinical review on dental tourism and barotrauma published on PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9880927/) explains that commercial aircraft cabin pressure changes can trigger barodontalgia (pressure-induced tooth pain) or barosinusitis, which may compromise a fresh sinus graft. The [UK General Dental Council (GDC)](https://www.gdc-uk.org/standards-guidance/information-for-patients-public/going-abroad-for-dental-treatment) also urges patients to budget contingency time in case healing takes longer than expected. Use this pre-booking checklist before purchasing flights:

items: Book flexible or changeable return tickets in case a lab adjustment or swelling check adds 48 hours
Count working days, excluding arrival day, departure day, Sundays, and Turkish public holidays
Schedule a mandatory final bite check at least 24 hours after permanent cementation
Never book a same-day flight immediately after extractions, implants, or sinus surgery
Keep prescribed analgesics, antibiotics, and written clinical notes in your cabin carry-on bag

faq.q: Can I finish 20 veneers in Türkiye in 5 days?
faq.a: Five calendar days rarely allows two separate laboratory try-ins and a post-bonding bite check, especially if a weekend falls in the middle. Eight to ten calendar days is far safer.

faq.q: Do Turkish dental clinics and labs work on weekends?
faq.a: Many clinics open on Saturdays for consultations or simple checks, but dental laboratories often close or run reduced shifts on Sundays. Always confirm exact lab working days before booking flights.

faq.q: How soon can I fly home after All-on-4 implant surgery?
faq.a: Clinical guidance sets 72 hours as the minimum wait after implant surgery, with five to seven days recommended so your surgeon can monitor peak swelling and check temporary bridge stability before you fly.

faq.q: Why is flying dangerous after a sinus lift?
faq.a: Cabin pressure changes during ascent and descent can create pressure differentials inside the sinus cavity (barosinusitis), risking membrane perforation, bleeding, or graft failure. Wait at least two weeks unless your surgeon advises otherwise.

faq.q: Should I plan sightseeing during a dental trip to Türkiye?
faq.a: Light, low-exertion walks work well on laboratory waiting days, but avoid strenuous tours, hammams, saunas, or swimming after oral surgery to reduce bleeding and infection risk.

faq.q: What if my bite still feels high on the day before my flight?
faq.a: Stay for an adjustment rather than hoping it settles at home. Flexible tickets and an extra buffer day protect you from paying out-of-pocket repairs—covered in our [Turkish dental warranty guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/dental-warranty-turkey).
